# Environmental change. Economic systems. Equitable development.

**360 Political Ecology (360PE)** connects environmental change, economics, political economy and social equity through accessible, evidence-informed analysis.

**Evidence · Ecology · Equity · Development**

[Read 360PE Review](publications.qmd){.pe-button}
:::

## Why 360PE exists

::: {.pe-home-grid}
::: {.pe-home-card}
### Mission

To generate and share credible, evidence-informed knowledge that supports more equitable, sustainable and resilient societies.
:::
::: {.pe-home-card}
### Purpose

To help researchers, policymakers, practitioners and the wider public understand environmental and development challenges, assess trade-offs and consider viable responses.
:::
:::

## How we work: from evidence to informed action

Our editorial approach moves from evidence to interpretation and policy dialogue. This is a **research communication pathway**, not a claim that every publication demonstrates policy impacts.

<div class="pe-work-grid" role="list" aria-label="360PE research communication pathway">
  <div class="pe-work-step" role="listitem"><span>01</span><strong>Data &amp; research</strong><p>Use credible scientific, institutional and field-based evidence.</p></div>
  <div class="pe-work-step" role="listitem"><span>02</span><strong>Critical analysis</strong><p>Assess competing explanations, limitations and uncertainties.</p></div>
  <div class="pe-work-step" role="listitem"><span>03</span><strong>Environmental justice lens</strong><p>Ask who benefits, who bears costs and whose voices are heard.</p></div>
  <div class="pe-work-step" role="listitem"><span>04</span><strong>Policy options</strong><p>Compare feasible, evidence-informed responses and trade-offs.</p></div>
  <div class="pe-work-step" role="listitem"><span>05</span><strong>Development implications</strong><p>Examine potential implications for equitable and sustainable outcomes.</p></div>
</div>

## What we study

Our publication spans ten interconnected thematic areas, from climate resilience to environmental law. Each 360PE Review article addresses at least one area.

::: {.pe-tiles}
::: {.pe-tile}
**Climate, energy and industrial transitions**

Climate adaptation; energy and resource economics; critical minerals and energy transitions.
:::
::: {.pe-tile}
**Justice, governance and ecosystems**

Environmental justice and health; political economy; biodiversity and ecosystems.
:::
::: {.pe-tile}
**Development, finance and international policy**

Sustainability, climate finance, Just Transition, and environmental law and treaties.
:::
:::

[Explore all ten official research areas →](topics.qmd)

## Join the conversation

360PE welcomes informed critique, research collaborations and constructive contributions. The publication was founded by **Dr. Amanfo Smart Edward, PhD**, and operates independently of any university or other institution.
